traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Rubus (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.4 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 87 records in 8 sources); trunks 0.4, branches 0.43. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: stamens numerous; pistils many, crowded on an elevated receptacle, each ovary superior. The counts belong to each species.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rubus by L. A. Alice et al. (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits aggregates of (1-)5-100 drupelets on the torus; leaves alternate on the stems (cauline); plants perennial (one annual species).

rules.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rubus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves palmately compound or ternate, the lateral leaflets stalked or nearly sessile and smaller than the end one; the 200 degree fan and the lowest leaflets at seven tenths of the end one are ours, read from the key's leaf characters and Himalayan blackberry's leaf as drawn.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Rubus by L. A. Alice et al. (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): the hypanthium usually and the sepals usually persist under the ripe fruit, usually turned back (reflexed); Flora of China vol. 9 (2003), genus Rubus: sepals persistent, erect or reflexed. A species whose sepals stay erect or fall says so.

appearance.organs.*.shape.spread.why: A bramble's palmate or ternate leaf holds its leaflets in a fan a little past a half circle, the end leaflet forward and the lowest pair out to the sides, not swept back round the stalk.

appearance.organs.*.shape.lowest.why: A bramble's side leaflets are smaller than its end one, the lowest pair smallest.
